title: JJ Bleday hits for cycle, Elly De La Cruz falls a triple short in Reds’ rout of D-Backs
content:
The Cincinnati Reds waited three years between cycles. They almost got another one two innings later.

Outfielder JJ Bleday became just the eighth Red to hit for the cycle and the second in three years when he hit for his first cycle Saturday night in an 11-5 win over the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field.

Bleday blasted his career-high 21st home run of the season in the sixth inning to complete his cycle — the franchise’s first since June 23, 2023, when Elly De La Cruz hit for the cycle in just the 15th game of his career. De La Cruz had a chance to join him in the top of the eighth, needing a triple to complete his own cycle, but struck out looking.

Bleday doubled in De La Cruz in the first inning, hit an RBI triple in the third, singled in the fourth and then homered to lead off the sixth. He later flew out in the seventh inning and struck out in the ninth, finishing the night 4-for-6 after coming into the game with just one hit in his previous 14 at-bats.

De La Cruz also finished 4-for-6, with two singles, a double and a homer.

Bleday’s home run was one of four for the Reds on Saturday, marking the 10th time they have hit four or more home runs in a game this season — the most in baseball.

De La Cruz homered in the fifth; rookie Héctor Rodríguez hit his first career home run in the seventh; and second baseman Matt McLain hit his 13th home run of the season in the eighth. Each of the Reds’ first three homers came off Zack Littell, a former Red who was released by the Washington Nationals on Aug. 7 and signed with the Diamondbacks on Aug. 10.

Bleday, 28, signed a one-year deal with the Reds this offseason after being non-tendered by the Athletics. After starting the season in the minors, Bleday was called up to the big leagues on April 25. He was selected National League Player of the Month for May after hitting .301/.387/.631 with eight home runs.
